note: The phone screen is right in every respect, the prompt wording included. The one thing this check called a fault this morning - the prompt reading 'Search work orders, parts...' instead of 'Search everything' - turns out to be exactly what the requirement asks for. The product is right and OUR CHECK is the thing that needs its wording corrected.
evidence:
THE REQUIREMENT, READ LIVE ON 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 from the Global Search product requirements page (Confluence 576978945, version 17), section 5.6 Mobile, says word for word:

  "On phones the search is a full-screen screen, not a centered modal: it replaces the page, has a Cancel action in the top bar next to the input, and no keyboard-hints footer. Placeholder copy: 'Search work orders, parts...'."

WHAT WAS SEEN on a phone-sized screen (390 by 844), build v26.36.7-29ca209: the search fills the whole screen, shows a Cancel action, shows no keyboard legend, replaces the row of nine tabs with a row of chips that appears only once words are typed, shows every matching line rather than the first five, keeps the type headings stuck to the top while scrolling, offers no Show all link, and does not scroll sideways. The prompt reads 'Search work orders, parts...'.

Every one of those matches the requirement, including the prompt. There is no fault here and no report is needed.

What needs to be done: the QA lead to allow this check's wording to be corrected. It currently asks for 'Search everything', which no version of the requirement asks for; the phrase came from an older draft. Until it is corrected the next person will fail this check again for the same wrong reason.

note: Correct on the part that the requirement actually states: there is no Show all on a phone. The other half - the arrow keys still moving a highlight - is not a fault. The requirement says keyboard use does not apply on a phone; it does not ask for it to be switched off. OUR CHECK turned 'does not apply' into 'must not happen', and that is the thing to correct.
evidence:
THE REQUIREMENT, READ LIVE ON 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 from the Global Search product requirements page (Confluence 576978945, version 17), section 5.6 Mobile, says word for word:

  "In the All view results are not capped per group and there is no Show all overflow - the user scrolls the full grouped list."
  "Deferred on mobile (v1): keyboard navigation (5.5), which does not apply."

WHAT WAS SEEN on a phone-sized screen (390 by 844), build v26.36.7-29ca209: there is no Show all link anywhere and no keyboard legend - both exactly as required. Pressing the down arrow does still move a highlight onto a result line.

WHY THAT IS NOT A FAULT: the requirement puts keyboard use outside this version on a phone and says it does not apply. It does not ask for the behaviour to be removed. A person holding a phone has no arrow key to press, so nothing a real user can do reaches it.

What needs to be done: the QA lead to allow this check's wording to be corrected, so it stops asking for arrow-key movement to be switched off - something no version of the requirement asks for.
